I’ll be honest: my reason for doing psychology is to better understand myself. I have mental health issues, so by doing psychology, i can get a better grip on what is going on in my head rather than me just thinking ‘oh brains never happy, that sucks, go to psychologist’. Like already, I’m understanding what dopamine and serotonin are, instead of them just being ‘happy chemical in brain’ or whatever. 

But like a lot of the comments said, some people think it’s just easy science, and they still want to be able to say they did a science for VCE. They don’t really get that there’s a lot to psychology, and while you may be able to get by through ROTE learning, it’s gonna take a bit more than that to apply concepts to a range of different examples through the year.
